display_name: Irene the Empress, the nun Xenia

names.form: Преп. царица Ирина, у монаштву названа Ксенија

names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 13 Αυγούστου, «Αγία Ειρήνη η βασιλίσσα, της διά του αγίου και αγγελικού σχήματος μετονομασθείσης Ξένης Mοναχής», with the rank word and the royal title left off. The page glosses the name as the one who has calm and makes calm of soul and spirit about her.

Her monastic name, read out of the same line of saint.gr for 13 Αυγούστου: «της διά του αγίου και αγγελικού σχήματος μετονομασθείσης Ξένης Mοναχής», renamed Xene by the holy and angelic habit. The notice repeats it, «μετονομασθείσα Ξένη».

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 26.08.2026 (13. август ст. ст.) — „Преп. царица Ирина, у монаштву названа Ксенија.“

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 13ης Αυγούστου — «Αγία Ειρήνη η βασιλίσσα, της διά του αγίου και αγγελικού σχήματος μετονομασθείσης Ξένης Mοναχής»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 13 Αυγούστου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing. The Serbian row already keeps her on the Julian 13 August, under the same two names, and the Greek calendar keeps her on the revised-julian 13 August, the same menologion number. The Greek notice is a full life where the Prologue's is a line: she lived in the twelfth century; Alexios Komnenos saw her beauty and virtue and married her to his son John, called Kaloioannes for his many virtues; she spent freely on works of mercy and went alone to poor huts; she built homes for the aged and hostels and endowed them; her husband died on campaign in Syria in 1143 and afterwards two of her four children; with the consent of her son the emperor Manuel she withdrew to the monastery of the Pantokrator and was tonsured, renamed Xene; she was buried in great simplicity as she had wished, having said shortly before her death that the empress Irene had died long ago and that only the nun Xene was left. The couplet calls her the foundress of her own monastery below. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence on the life page. The page prints no apolytikion and no kontakion, so no hymn is added.

death.note: saint.gr: «Η Αγία Ειρήνη έζησε τον 12ο αιώνα μ.Χ.». The page gives no year of her birth or death; the only year in the notice is 1143, when her husband died on campaign in Syria, and she was tonsured and died after that. Read 1 October 2026.
